Great for travel, too

Great camping pillow, I can blow it up with 3 or 4 easy breaths and it has a nice deflate lock feature that you can hold to release a little air, or click into place so it deflates all the way. It rolls up well and actually fits back into the carrying case it came in. The cover is surprisingly soft and smooth, and always feels cold in a good way. I got this for camping, but because it rolls back up so nicely it’s definitely going to be my go-to travel pillow for flights. I’ve had no issues with it deflating over long periods of use, even when I toss and turn a bit. The air lock system is really sturdy and works consistently, it’s not one of those awkward plastic nipples that leaks and hurts to blow into. I would absolutely recommend this. 





To Whom It May Concern in the Shadeco Hiring Team, 

Oh, whoops, sorry - I just saw you asked to keep it casual and cool, let me try that again…
 

Yo! Whatsup Shadeco hiring team! 

Yikes, too much? That felt like too much. Sorry, last time starting over I promise. 


Hello there! 

Is this where I ask for free sunglasses? You know what, nevermind, let me introduce myself first.

My name is Marcus, and if you’re reading this it means you’ve boldly decided to look into me as a candidate despite the fact that I answered “no” to your question about experience. Let me convince you right now why you made a great decision to open this cover letter. 

It’s fun, full of personality, and vulnerable 
It makes some worthy points - both by demonstration and argumentation - that I may be a good fit for this role (more on the latter later) 
You’re already almost done reading it! 

My argument is this: I do not have 3 years experience (bad) but I do have 20 years writing skits, screenplays, essays, feedback to Oscar-winning writers, and now gag cover letters (good). I also have 6+ wonderful years together with my beautiful Art Director wife. So while other copywriters may be able to check “yes” on your box, how many of them can boast years of asking “how was your day, honey?” and hearing exactly what makes for a good copywriter from the POV of their closest peer? 

Much like the octopus-fighting pirate in my illustration, I feel I’ve taken my best shot here - so all I can say is I look forward to hearing back soon.

Ahoy and Fair Winds, 
Marcus

When a pilot activates their ejection seat, the canopy of their aircraft is blown off, and an explosive cartridge detonates under the seat. 

The explosion launches the seat out of the aircraft along a set of guide rails. 

After ejection, an underseat rocket ignites, lifting the pilot even higher to a safe altitude above the failing aircraft. 

Then, a drogue parachute fires out of the chair, stabilizing the pilot’s fall. 

Once stable, the pilot’s parachute activates, the seat is separated, and the pilot descends to safety. 




At Just 8 Years Old, an Elephant Saved Her Life

She was just 8 years old when an elephant saved her life. 

Her family was on vacation when a magnitude-9.1 earthquake struck under the sea. 

Thinking nothing of it, her family continued their day as usual.

She was riding on the back of the elephant when suddenly, the ocean pulled back, revealing bumpy sand and fish.

She had no idea what was happening, but the elephant’s animal instincts kicked in. 

The tsunami rushed in, flooding the surrounding lagoons, but the elephant brought her safely inland, saving her life.

Dear Creative Giant Team,

My name is Marcus and I’m reaching out because I’ve recently done creative giant myself. At the end of 2023, after over 4 years working in entertainment, I decided to pack my things and move to the world of advertising. I spent the last 18 months studying copywriting at Creative Portfolio Academy, and now I’m looking to start my new career here in Los Angeles. 

While looking for potential landing pads for my leap of faith, Creative Giant stood out for one reason: you guys are clearly makers. I’ve long been a figure-outer, a build-the-plane-while-landing-it type, someone who does something first, then figures out how to do it after. That doesn’t mean I underestimate the value of a good plan, it just means I understand the creative process as an exercise in exploration and discovery, not as a study of instruction following. 

Clearly, Creative Giant holds those same values. If you find yourself in need of a copywriter, content creator, or pair of hands willing to learn any ropes - please keep me in mind for any future opportunities that may arise. 

All the best,
Marcus

I am writing to you today with a heavy heart. My entire life I have aspired to be a do-gooder, a benefactor to society, a samaritan worthy of praise… but hard times have fallen on us all, and so here I am in the inbox of “RebelMedia” - a company whose values seem to fly in the face of everything I have ever stood for. 

If you can look past the dozens of kittens I have rescued from burning homes and the innumerable old ladies I have helped cross busy streets, I actually think we could be a good match. 

In particular, I’m intrigued by your emphasis on content, which many traditional big agencies are - forgive me - no good at. In my time at Creative Portfolio Academy, I found that even the instructors and leadership were behind the 8 ball on teaching content, treating it as unnecessary bells and whistles for a portfolio at best, or ignoring it completely at worst. So naturally, I’m seeking to lean in to content creation and kickstart my career somewhere that doesn’t neglect it or write it off, even if that place is no good. 

The one thing that might make me a no good candidate is that I am staunchly LA based, but you could say I’m bi-coastal curious. 

Yours in debauchery, 
Marcus

Dear Atlas Agency hiring team, 

I am not a religious man, but I am a well-read man, and so I am familiar with the source text of your agency’s namesake not from a spiritual background but from a literary one. It’s my understanding that Goliath, shipwrecked and separated from his crew, awashes on an island of teeny tiny people and soon becomes entangled (literally and figuratively) in their affairs. 

Through his adventures and travels we’re treated to insights on the human condition, the nature of kindness, and the petty things we spend our lives arguing about. All noble ideas to interrogate, to be sure, and themes I see reflected in your agency’s work. It’s my goal to spend my life like it’s one of Goliath’s travels: making giant-sized observations about the world not from a sidelined perspective, but from getting tangled up right in the center of things. 

I believe this approach to creativity is well-suited to your company, and it would be my honor to wash up upon your shores. Please don’t hesitate to reach out should you have any questions about my resume, portfolio, or extensive knowledge of literature and the arts as I believe I have demonstrated in the cover letter. 

Thank you for your consideration, 
Marcus Torne

More than half of vape users want to give it up, but quitting cold turkey (the most common approach) is only successful around 4% of the time. 

Failing that, strategies get rather clinical. Trigger lists, support networks, even therapy can all be successful if attempted, but feel like big, medical undertakings that might scare off the casual vaper who knows better, but doesn’t want to address the habit like the disease it is. 

So instead of asking quit-pilled users to come to us, we meet them where they’re at by launching Hot Turkey, a line of terrible-tasting vapes for users who want to quit.

These comedically gnarly vapes deliver a touch of nicotine so users can gently curb their addiction by making the experience unpleasant. Essentially, we’re turning quitting into a joke to lower the barrier to entry for the majority of vapers seeking an offramp from addiction. 

Wanna quit? Hate the hit.

Milk Brief - 

Milk the Moment
Play off the societal value on attention, and increasing sense that attention - good or bad - is always a valuable thing to obtain. Drinking milk raises an eyebrow. In other words, people notice it when you do - in other words - it gets you attention. We argue a huge benefit of milk is simply the looks you get when you do so. Revel in the incredulity, the judgement, and shock, awe, or even disgust of those around you. Milk gets eyes looking your way, and that’s all that matters. So, when you order a glass of the cool white, milk the moment and soak up the attention. 

Could work as a tagline first campaign i.e. Milk the moment… when you tell the barista cow milks if fine (and the AD could be the weird looks people give) 

Milk the moment… when 2% shows up alongside your filet mignon 

Milk the moment… when lunch beers aren’t the only tall glass on your corner of the pub 

Milk the moment… when you realize your drink order’s a headline in her groupchat 

Milk the moment… when popcorn isn’t your only movie go-to 

Milk the moment… when your idea of a night cap is a nighty-night cap 

Milk the moment… when your mustache outshines his 

Milk the moment… when you see their udder shock 

Around the time “Do it for the Vine” entered our shared vernacular, humanity became obsessed with attention. It’s now the social currency we deal in, and folks go to any expense to get it - good, bad, or neutral. 

When children drink milk, no one bats an eye. When adults do it, however, they’re freaks worthy of ire. Pre-”do it for the Vine” you wouldn’t want to catch those looks. But now? That’s free money baby. So when you go out to Benihana for your friend’s bday, steal the show (and their attention) by ordering a big tall glass of milk to go with your yakisoba and milk the moment when all eyes are on you - who cares if they’re filled with disgust? 


The Least Transparent Drink

Unlike the overwhelming majority of drinks, milk is opaque. You can’t see right through it, it obscures vision, could be hiding something? There’s a huge cultural push for “transparency” in all things, but the truth seems more obscured than ever, and even things that seem simple and clear-cut on the face are never so easily defined and explained. Can milk play into this tension? It’s straight up opaque. There’s no telling what’s on the other side of it. Can it tongue-and-cheek own being opaque and the least transparent of any drink? Maybe winking and nodding to how simple and unprocessed of a product it is? Haven’t landed the ship here, but some interesting thematic territory to explore potentially. 

Same Day Delivery, 100 years before Amazon
Milk - famously - was delivered door-to-door fresh everyday by handy men as far back as the late 1800s. I assume. This predates any modern evidence that Amazon existed as a company, and certainly predates their renowned same-day or next-day shipping. Is there a play here to lean into late 2000s early 2010s millennial hipsterisms as milk having done something before it was cool? Enough time may have passed that now Milk is on the outside, a moniker of counter-culture avant-garde classic hipster ideology in the exact same way soy milk or cashew milk or almond milk or what have you was a moniker of hipsterism and a sign of things to come as far back as the early internet rage-comic days of the early 2010s. 

Even our haters love us 
Famously, no one loves dairy products more than the lactose intolerant. There’s endless memes about how they don’t let their body’s physical inability to digest milk stop them from doing exactly that. There’s an obvious tension there - maybe we could partner with Lactaid? Like, milk is so eminently loveable that even those who can’t tolerate it can’t resist it? Or maybe it’s like a bad-boy type thing. Like, “I know you’re bad for me… but I just can’t resist you” type of tension - which might work overtime given milk is such so bland/boring/the opposite of edgy. Playing milk as the “bad boy” of beverages could really work here based on this intolerance insight.

Cereve / Lotion brand idea: a pair of dishwashing rubber gloves with built in dispenser/pores for lotion to both protect hands when they’re most vulnerable: while washing dishes - but also to solve the problem of trying to slip on a dry latex glove that just wants to catch and pull at your skin. 














Guinness - The Sliding G Pint	

“Splitting the G” has quickly become a favorite game for Guinness drinkers, but is difficult to master. So we’ll create a rigged pint glass where the “G” is on a track so you can slide it to meet the beer wherever your sip lands.


The CeraVe Dish Gloves 

Washing dishes dries out your skin, but putting on dish gloves is difficult. 

The solution isn’t rocket science, it’s the type of brilliance that works in its simplicity. 

	“Creativity is the sudden cessation of stupidity” 

Two birds, one stone: put lotion in your dish gloves. This allows hands to slip in easily, making a task that typically dries hands out into one that moisturizes and rejuvenates them.

We took the idea one half step beyond pumping the lotion straight in (though in all honesty this would work, too) and invented a thin mesh pore system that evenly distributes a thin film of lotion throughout the interior of each glove with a refillable port for repeated use.

If this feels obvious or like low hanging fruit, that’s because it is. I ask you: did you think of it though? 




Idea for car brand - make carpet and leather seats pattern that looks cool and classy, but whose main point is to disguise crumbs and trash so even when your car isn’t clean it looks cool 


Toyota - Kid Camo

Kids and clean cars are diametrically opposed beings. 

Sure, there are little vacuums and spot-cleaners for floor mats - some car brands have gone so far as to include built-in vacuums in new minivan models - but these are temporary solutions and every parent knows whatever state of cleanliness they achieve is fleeting. 

So instead of tasking parents with the sisyphean job of keeping their cars clean, Toyota invented the Kid Camo finish for the interiors of their SUVs and Minivans. The specially designed pattern serves as a stylish camouflage for the spills, crumbs, and trash any parent’s car is sure to accumulate. With Kid Camo interiors, your car looks fabulous in any state of cleanliness, so you can keep your hand vac charging uselessly behind your laundry machine.
